modelResponse.episodeSummary: 31yo male, Sinus Rhythm, stable hemodynamics, presenting with diffuse ST elevation and PR depression.
keyECGEvidence: Diffuse concave (upward-scooping) ST elevation 1-2 mm in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, V3-V6
PR-segment depression in leads II, III, aVF, V4-V6
No reciprocal ST depression in any other lead
modelResponse.mechanism: Inflammation of the pericardium causing diffuse epicardial injury and junctional-type electrical changes (PR segment deviation).
contributingFactors: Recent upper respiratory infection 1 week ago
Elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 4.8 mg/dL HIGH, ESR 38 mm/hr HIGH, WBC 11.2 10^3/uL mild HIGH)

rejectedAlternatives.why: ST elevation is diffuse and concave rather than localized to a vascular territory; lacks reciprocal ST depression; pain is pleuritic and relieved by leaning forward; no pathologic Q waves.

While possible given the recent URI, the classic ECG pattern of diffuse concave ST elevation and PR depression is more pathognomonic for pericarditis; troponin T 0.03 ng/mL is only mildly elevated, suggesting minimal myocardial involvement.

recommendedActions: Initiate NSAID therapy (e.g., Ibuprofen or Aspirin) as per clinical guidelines for acute pericarditis
Consider Colchicine to reduce recurrence risk
Monitor Troponin T levels to assess for progression to myocarditis
Avoid excessive NSAID use if renal function changes, though Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL is currently normal
Monitor for signs of cardiac tamponade (e.g., hypotension, increased JVD, muffled heart sounds)
uncertainty: Degree of myocardial involvement (myocarditis) cannot be fully ruled out without serial troponins and potentially cardiac MRI.
